A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable main text, equations and complete appendices. v2 retains the theoretical material in Appendices A-F and adds experiments and a checklist.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical guarantees, mathematical counterexamples and proofs, but no original empirical results, including in its appendices.

after.justification: Appendix G reports original Gaussian, Exponential and Beta simulations in Figures 1-4, with values averaged over 50 runs. These qualify despite contradictory experimental NA answers in the checklist.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sampling, data accumulation and maximum-likelihood objective. Appendix G evaluates numerical fitting as an implementation variant without revising the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical evaluation. v2 establishes empirical coverage through density-estimation simulations using one-dimensional Gaussian, Exponential and Beta(theta,1) data.

E2.justification: Figures 1-3 newly compare closed-form exact MLE with numerically optimized MLE. This introduces a limited comparison between solver variants; v1 contains no empirical comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces 100-iteration simulations, parameter-norm error, error relative to iteration 1, sample-size variation and a Beta parameter sweep. Sample sizes are inconsistent: the prose specifies 20, 50 and 100, while Figures 1-3 label 20, 100 and 500.

E4.justification: v2 adds two substantive analyses absent from v1: whether numerical optimization changes iterative stability (Figures 1-3), and how varying the Beta ground-truth parameter affects error amplification (Figure 4), intended to probe smoothness sensitivity.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that experimental values are averaged over 50 runs. It supplies no seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests; v1 has no empirical run statistics.

E6.justification: Figures 1-4 add empirical findings of similar qualitative stability for exact and optimized MLE and greater Beta error amplification at smaller theta0. The text reports 3.27-fold growth at theta0=0.1; its stated 1.25-fold growth at theta0=1 conflicts with Figure 4's curve ending closer to 1.1.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1-3, Theorems 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2, and the proofs in Appendices A-F are substantively unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects a terminal-time index typo and makes existing high-probability qualifications explicit.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the non-asymptotic consistency guarantee and both rapid-collapse counterexamples. The claimed necessity of structural assumptions beyond MLE consistency and the novelty claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of neural-network applicability and possible extensions to approximate MLE. New Section 5.3 emphasizes the artificial counterexamples and conjectures that nonsmoothness is central; Appendix G interprets its Beta results as supporting this explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly documents scipy.optimize.minimize, negative-log-likelihood fitting and ground-truth parameters. Optimizer initialization and tolerances are unspecified, and checklist items 4-8 inconsistently mark experimental reporting as NA.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive distinction between Dohmatob et al. (2025)'s non-iterative regression setting and accumulating-data analyses. The cited-work set is retained; the changed title of He et al. (2025) refers to the same arXiv work.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction, expands explanations, standardizes theorem references and adds Section 5.3, Appendix G and the NeurIPS checklist. The existing theoretical narrative and section ordering remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four empirical figures absent from v1: three paired exact/optimized-MLE displays and a Beta sensitivity plot. These introduce substantial new visual evidence; the retained theoretical pages mainly undergo text reflow.

improvement.justification: Figures 1-3 provide limited empirical evidence about numerical fitting, a practical issue unexplored in v1, while Section 5.3 clarifies the counterexamples' artificial nature. These modest gains supplement unchanged theory. Conflicting sample counts, the Figure 4/text discrepancy and contradictory checklist answers limit confidence in the added evidence and its reproducibility.
